title: Analysis of Radiation Exposure During Ventral Spondylodesis Using a Fully Motorized C-Arm Compared to a Non-Motorized C-Arm
summary:
Spinal fusion (spondylodesis) is an established surgical procedure used to treat various spinal disorders. Intraoperative imaging of the surgical site is routinely performed using X-ray technology. Continuous advancements in imaging techniques and systems aim to reduce the risks associated with harmful radiation exposure for both surgical staff and patients.
Among these advancements are new motorized C-arm systems, which are capable of storing and automatically returning to predefined spatial positions. This functionality may allow for faster repositioning and potentially fewer X-ray images to achieve optimal visualization.
The aim of this study is to determine whether radiation exposure during minimally invasive spinal fusion is lower when using a fully motorized C-arm compared to a conventional non-motorized C-arm.
conditions: Pathologies requiring anterior spinal fusion with disc replacement at L1–L5.

interventions.name: Ventral spondylodesis using a fully motorized C-arm
Ventral spondylodesis using a non-motorized C-arm

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with an indication for anterior spinal fusion with disc replacement in the lumbar spine (L1–L5)
- Written informed consent for the surgical procedure
- Written informed consent to participate in this study
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients with impaired or questionable capacity to provide informed consent
- Patients in whom, during the surgical procedure, the availability of the following devices is limited: non-motorized C-arm Cios Spin / motorized C-arm Ciartic Move (Siemens) / live dosimeter (Raysafe)
